\section{Setup}

Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a $n$-dimensional lattice polytope
with volume $V_{P}$. Let $\mathrm{d}\sigma$ be the lattice boundary
measure on $\partial P$, which is defined as follows. For each facet
$F\subset\partial P$ spanning affine subspace $\mathrm{Aff}(F)$,
$\mathrm{d}\sigma|_{F}$ is the Lebesgue measure normalized by the
lattice $\mathrm{Aff}(F)\cap\mathbb{Z}^{n}$. If 
\[
F=\left\{ x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\mid\left\langle x,v_{F}\right\rangle +a_{F}\ge0\right\} ,
\]
where $v_{F}\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}$ is primitive. Then $\mathrm{d}\sigma|_{F}=\mathrm{d}s/\left|v_{F}\right|$,
$\mathrm{d}s$ is the Euclidean boundary measure. 

\section{Question }

Let $\mathcal{C}(P)$ be the space of convex functions on $P$ (continuous
up to $\partial P$). Consider a functional 
\[
\Psi(f)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{P}f^{2}\mathrm{d}x+\int_{\partial P}f\ \mathrm{d}\sigma,\ f\in\mathcal{C}(P).
\]
Known facts: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Psi$ admits a unique minimizer $\psi=-\Theta_{P}\in\mathcal{C}(P)$,
which is continuous up to $\partial P$. Refer to \cite{Szekelyhidi}
and \cite{Sheng-Yao}. We call $\Theta_{P}$ the optimal test-function,
which equals to $B$ in \cite{Szekelyhidi}. 
\item variational inequality: $\int_{\partial P}f\mathrm{d}\sigma\ge\int_{P}f\Theta_{P},\ \text{for }\forall f\in\mathcal{C}(P)$.
$\int_{\partial P}\Theta_{P}\mathrm{d}\sigma=\int_{P}\Theta^{2}_{P}$. 
\item $\Theta_{P}$ is the unique element with minimal $L^{2}$-norm in
the set 
\[
\mathcal{S}(P)=\left\{ \theta\in L^{2}(P)\mid\int_{\partial P}f\mathrm{d}\sigma\ge\int_{P}f\theta,\ \forall f\in\mathcal{C}(P)\right\} .
\]
\item $\sup_{P}\Theta_{P}=\sup_{\partial P}\Theta_{P}>0$. 
\item \cite{Li-Zhou} $\psi=-\Theta_{P}$ satisfies the homogenous Monge--Ampère
equation in the sense of Alexandrov. Precisely, for any compact set
$K\subset\mathrm{int}P$, the Lebesgue measure $\left|\partial u(K)\right|=0$. 
\end{enumerate}
Question: Is $\Theta_{P}$ piecewisely affine or not ?
